title: fix(flow): use the shared dashboard sign-in UI
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replaces Flow’s plain HTML login with the shared `DashboardSignIn` used by KPI, Observability and Economics: matching layout, logo, fonts, theme toggle, button and error messages.
- Serves sign-in assets from the Worker before any reviewer container starts. Keeps ordinary-account access and sends embedded Admin recovery to the canonical top-level login.
- Adds browser coverage for light/dark layouts at 320, 375 and 1280px, error recovery, preserved Flow selections, shared-session logout and iframe navigation.
- Validation: 88 UI tests, 32 shared-auth tests and 9 Flow gateway tests; UI/Flow typechecks and builds; visual inspection; Wrangler/Docker packaging dry-run.

gist.headline: Flow joins the same front door
gist.blurb: Flow’s sign-in now looks like the rest of the dashboard family, down to the theme toggle and error messages. Even the login screen arrives before the reviewer container wakes up.
gist.summary: Flow replaces its plain HTML login with the shared DashboardSignIn used by KPI, Observability and Economics, and serves sign-in assets directly from the Worker before a reviewer container starts.
gist.impact: Flow reviewers get a consistent sign-in screen across light and dark themes, while ordinary-account access remains available and embedded Admin recovery opens the canonical top-level login.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Flow as a cozy retro dashboard with a welcoming shared sign-in screen, a small theme-toggle icon, and neighboring dashboard windows that match its look. Polli, wearing a tiny keyring, opens the dashboard door; code-plants and lime-green light keep the scene warm. No separate Flow mascot is indicated.

Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes; prominent lime green (#ecf874), warm cream background, and dark purple (#110518) outlines.
